question: At the time of colonial period, the Asaf Jahi dynasty was established in _______.
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Hyderabad**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Asaf Jahi dynasty** was established in **Hyderabad** during the **colonial period**.
 
• The dynasty was founded by **Mir Qamar-ud-Din Khan**, also known as **Nizam-ul-Mulk**, in the year **1724**.
 
• The Asaf Jahi rulers were referred to as the **Nizams**, and Hyderabad became the capital of their kingdom.
 
• The Nizam of Hyderabad was one of the most powerful rulers in **India's princely states** during the British colonial era.
 
• Hyderabad under the Nizams was known for its **rich cultural heritage**, including **architecture, literature, and art.**
 
• The Asaf Jahi dynasty played a significant role in shaping the **political and cultural landscape** of South India.
 
• Hyderabad's landmarks like the **Charminar** and the **Golconda Fort** were deeply associated with the city's historical significance.
 
• The Nizams of Hyderabad maintained a unique status as a **semi-autonomous princely state** under British rule.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Punjab**__

 __
 
• **Punjab** was primarily ruled by the **Sikh Empire** during the early colonial period under **Maharaja Ranjit Singh**.
 
• It was annexed by the British after the **Second Anglo-Sikh War** in **1849**.
 
• The region is known for its **agricultural significance** and the **Indus Valley Civilization**.
 
 
 
• **Bengal**__
 __
 
• **Bengal** was a prominent province under **British rule** and was the center of the **British East India Company's operations** in India.
 
• The **Battle of Plassey** in **1757** marked the beginning of British dominance in Bengal.
 
• It is known for its **literary and cultural contributions** during the **Indian Renaissance**.
 
 
 
• **Mysore**__
 
 
• **Mysore** was ruled by the **Wodeyar dynasty** and later by **Tipu Sultan**, known as the **Tiger of Mysore**.
 
• Tipu Sultan was a prominent figure who resisted British colonial expansion in the late **18th century**.
 
• Mysore is famous for its **palaces**, such as the **Mysore Palace**, and its contributions to **Indian classical music**.
